instructions: Stripe's validated OAuth for tooling is CLI pairing: the browser shows a pairing code and approving it is the whole consent — no keys are typed or pasted anywhere.
The manual equivalent is installing the Stripe CLI (docs.stripe.com/stripe-cli) and running `stripe login` yourself.
Stay in test mode while building; the pairing is test-mode by default.
The hosted Stripe MCP can additionally be authorized from the host for in-chat Stripe tools; it is optional and not required for provisioning.

instructions: Provisioning runs through the paired CLI: the webhook endpoint for `/stripe/webhook` is created and its signing secret goes straight into the Convex deployment env without ever being printed.
Prices are a product decision, not a setup step: when the price is chosen, run `pnpm stripe:provision --plan pro --usd <amount>` and the price id is stored as STRIPE_PRICE_PRO.

The API secret key is the one human-held value: run `pnpm secret:set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` in your own terminal. It prompts with hidden input and pipes the key into the Convex env — never chat, never shell history, never .env.local.
Complete one sandbox checkout and confirm entitlement changes from the webhook, not the return URL.

instructions: Linear's agent-tool path is the host-managed MCP authorization: the hosted server at mcp.linear.app uses OAuth with dynamic client registration, so approving in the browser is the whole consent and no API key is ever handled.

A host that already carries Linear through its own installed plugin or connector is already authorized: continue on that connection; never install, reconfigure, or disconnect the host's plugin to make the project catalog win.
Authorize only the Linear workspace this product's tracking should live in.
Limited scopes grant read-only access; mirroring the work queue needs issue read and write.
After browser authorization returns, ask the agent to make one read-only Linear MCP call (list teams) before resuming.
Pick or create the Linear team and project that mirror this product; both are visible in the Linear sidebar and need no API key.
The durable queue stays the source of truth: `pnpm agent:work` state drives Linear, never the reverse. The agent mirrors queue items to Linear issues through the MCP so a person can watch progress.

Issue titles and bodies carry contract-level summaries, acceptance criteria, status, and gate evidence only. Prompts, transcripts, credentials, webhook secrets, and personal account details never enter an issue.
Record only safe identifiers (team key, project and issue IDs) under `.agent-state/`; cancel the connection with `pnpm connect cancel` to stop mirroring at any time.

instructions: Netlify's validated OAuth for tooling is the CLI: `netlify login` opens a browser authorization page and approving it is the whole consent — no token is typed or pasted.
The manual equivalent is installing the Netlify CLI (docs.netlify.com/cli/get-started) and running `netlify login` yourself.
The credential lands in the CLI's own machine-local config, outside this repository.

run.why: Install the official Netlify CLI if missing, then authenticate: the browser opens an authorization page and the command waits for your approval. No token is typed or pasted.

instructions: The whole path is the terminal: `netlify init` creates the site and links this repository, `netlify env:set` configures it, `netlify deploy --prod` ships. No dashboard step stands between a fresh clone and a live URL.

`netlify.toml` is the deployment and is committed: its build command must run `npx convex deploy --cmd 'pnpm build'` so backend and frontend ship together. Netlify treats the file as authoritative, so it overrides the dashboard.

Netlify holds `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` and public keys only — set them with `netlify env:set <NAME> --secret`. Every backend secret stays in the prod Convex deployment env, never in Netlify or `netlify.toml`.
Secret values never appear in `netlify.toml`; it is committed, so a value written into it is published.

probes.label: Netlify deploys Convex and Next.js together

run.why: Create the Netlify site and link this repository from the terminal; it may open a browser to authorize site creation.

Ship the committed netlify.toml topology: it runs `npx convex deploy --cmd 'pnpm build'` so backend and frontend ship together.

revocation.why: Remove the Netlify CLI credential from this machine.

revocation.text: Revoke the authorization in the Netlify dashboard under User settings → Applications, and delete the site if it should not exist.
